As it warms, VO_2 becomes more metallic and its emissivity rises significantly. That means, for a given tempertaure difference ΔT, the radiative heat flux from the sample becomes larger once VO_2 is in or near its thermochromic transition. At low temperatures, before the transition, VO_2 stays in its insulating state and its emissivity is low and stable, this makes the forward heat flux very similar ot the reverse heat flux.

The only hot surface is the opposing plate. Radiative flux from a hot object onto a surface with unchanging emissivity produces an exchange that scales in a predictable, smooth way with ΔT and results in an effectively constant radiative thermal conductance. There is no switching transition on the VO_2 side in reverse bias, so rectification does not occur in this direction.
These two modes together means, when ΔT is below the VO_2 transition range on the forward side, VO_2 behaves similarly in both directions, meaning the forward and reverse heat fluxes are nearly equal. For example, Staphylococcus OTUs in the lung microbiome have been associated with faster disease progression, and lower gut OTU richness has been linked to more severe inflammatory disease phenotypes and blistering diseases, where patients showed reduced gut microbiota diversity and richness compared with healthy controls.
